testcase.name: OK: a verified identity creates one DRAFT agency and one ACTIVE OWNER membership in one transaction
DENY: unverified identity → 403 NOT_AUTHORIZED IDENTITY_UNVERIFIED; unauthenticated → 401; a second DRAFT for the same creator → 429 ADMISSION_LIMITED DRAFT_AGENCY_EXISTS
RACE: identical retry replays the same agency; same key with another displayName → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; crash before COMMIT leaves nothing; response lost after COMMIT is recovered by the key
OK: an OPERATOR creates a client; two clients may share a label and keep distinct ids

OK (deployment path): CreateClient records the end-client processing authority in its own unit of work — an agency created through the route creates its first client with nothing recorded beforehand; its reference binds a second workspace; another agency cannot record or use it
DENY: member of another agency → 404; VIEWER → 403 ROLE_INSUFFICIENT; processingAuthorityRef of another agency → 400 UNKNOWN_REFERENCE
RACE: identical retry replays; conflicting same key → 409; crash at the commit boundary leaves no client and no event
OK: an ADMIN archives an ACTIVE client; CreateProject on it is then refused; projects, revisions, approvals and receipts remain
DENY: OPERATOR → 403; foreign client → 404; stale expectedVersion → 409 STALE_VERSION with current

RACE: two archive calls with the same expectedVersion → one 200, one 409; identical retry replays; the same key with another expectedVersion or another client → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a crash before COMMIT leaves the client ACTIVE and the same key then archives it; a response lost after COMMIT is recovered by the key
OK: an OPERATOR creates a CLEAN project on an ACTIVE client with an offered capability; the response lists readiness blockers
DENY: foreign/wrong role → 404/403; HUBSPOT with no offered capability → 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE MODE_NOT_OFFERED; HUBSPOT without targetInstanceRef → 400; archived client → 409

RACE: identical retry replays; conflicting same key → 409; a crash before COMMIT commits nothing; a unit of work interrupted between the project insert and the revision insert commits nothing and the same key then creates the pair once; a project row without its revision cannot commit (deferred FK)

RACE: a capability suspension racing CreateProject — the project holds the mode's transition lock to COMMIT: a suspension that comes second waits for the project; one committed first refuses it 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE

RACE: an agency transition racing CreateProject — the project holds the agency's transition lock to COMMIT: a closure that comes second waits for the project; one committed first refuses it 409 AGENCY_NOT_OPEN
N3 RACE: a capability suspension queued behind an in-flight project is never overtaken — a project requested after it waits behind the suspension and is refused 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE
N3 RACE: an agency closure queued behind an in-flight project is never overtaken — a project requested after it waits behind the closure and is refused 409 AGENCY_NOT_OPEN
OK: an OPERATOR revises a VALIDATED plan; predecessor SUPERSEDED, successor VALIDATION_REQUIRED with a new body hash; the impact map names the invalidated receipt
DENY: APPROVER → 403; foreign plan → 404; expectedVersion of a superseded plan → 409 STALE_VERSION with successorId; patch naming an unknown candidate → 400
RACE: two RevisePlan calls with expectedVersion 2 — one 201, one 409 STALE_VERSION carrying successorId

RACE: two revisions on one version → one successor; identical retry replays; the same key with another patch → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; crash leaves the predecessor unsuperseded and the same key then revises it once

APPROVED: revising an approved plan takes the approval's controller and reconciled consequences; the approval is withdrawn with its own event in the same transaction, so no live approval remains on the SUPERSEDED plan
RACE: RevisePlan of an APPROVED plan and WithdrawApproval serialize on the plan lock — one of them ends the approval, once
DENY (typed patch): each compiler rejection answers its own reason and the same code on the field; only a reference that does not resolve is UNKNOWN_REFERENCE
OK: an APPROVER with a fresh step-up approves a VALIDATED plan whose receipt, source and target are current; the approval hash binds the named preimage

DENY: OPERATOR → 403; foreign → 404; stale/missing step-up → 403 ASSURANCE_REQUIRED; stale receipt → 422 PLAN_NOT_VALIDATED; disclosuresHash computed without the CLEAR set → 409 STALE_VERSION mismatch [disclosuresHash]; EXPIRED source → 422 SOURCE_EXPIRED; superseded target → 422 TARGET_STALE

RACE: two approvers on one version → one 201, one 409; identical retry replays; conflicting → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT; a crash before COMMIT leaves the plan VALIDATED with no approval and the same key then approves it once
RACE: two ApprovePlan calls — one 201, one 409; no approval of a superseded body
the approval binds its source and target through the planHash the approver names (the interim binding of the manual-10 / catalogue conflict, open question Q9)

RACE: a source expiry racing ApprovePlan — the approval holds the sealed revision's transition lock to COMMIT: an expiry that comes second waits and then reads the approval; an expiry committed first is refused 422 SOURCE_EXPIRED

RACE: a target-contract supersession racing ApprovePlan — the approval holds the contract's transition lock to COMMIT: a supersession that comes second waits and then reads the approval; one committed first is refused 422 TARGET_STALE

N3 RACE: a source expiry queued behind an in-flight approval is never overtaken — an approval requested after it, of another plan on the same source, waits behind the expiry and is refused 422 SOURCE_EXPIRED

N4: the target currency is the plan's own project's contract — superseding it refuses the approval 422 TARGET_STALE even while another project of the agency holds a current contract with the same body hash
N9: a plan of one project can never be bound to another project's sealed source or confirmed target — the plan itself is refused at insert, so no approval can bind them

N10: the planHash an approval binds is recomputed from the stored body — a plan whose stored hash is not the digest of its body is refused 422 INTEGRITY_FAILURE BODY_DIGEST_MISMATCH and nothing is approved
OK: the approving actor withdraws; approval carries withdrawn_at/by/reason, plan WITHDRAWN; the outbox routes EXECUTION_CONTROL; completed external actions are listed separately
DENY: VIEWER → 403; another APPROVER → 403 NOT_APPROVAL_CONTROLLER; foreign → 404; plan not APPROVED → 409 PRECONDITION_FAILED; stale version → 409 STALE_VERSION
RACE: two withdrawals → one 200, one 409; identical retry replays; a withdrawal cannot be undone (KA004)
OK (reason label): the withdrawal reason is the registry's label — 'Customer asked us to stop' is accepted, stored and answered verbatim, and never copied into an event payload
configuration: every variable is validated and a missing or malformed one refuses the start by name, never by value; the pool ceiling is a required input
authentication of this edition: the LOCAL bearer-token file is a closed document; SANDBOX and LIVE refuse to start without the Identity Platform verifier (I-INT-3)
bootstrap on a real cluster: migrations on start as the owner (idempotent), the verified runtime pool, a real socket serving a command, and a clean close; privileged logins refuse the start
R3: agency A's runtime role cannot occupy the next version of B's client; B's owner then archives it through CMD010 (200, version 2)
R4: a client created through CMD009 journals its label; the control pool reads the journal's metadata of that entry but never its response
R11: plan X approved through CMD025; plan Y cannot be pointed at X's approval, and CMD025 then approves Y with an approval of its own
R14/R30: the request-handler role cannot mint the evidence CMD025 checks — a step-up proof or a VALID receipt — while the verifier's proof and the validator's receipt admit the approval
same key + different body → 409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT and no effect
same key + same body → 200/201 replayed:true with the original body
response lost after commit → retry with the same key returns the journaled result
concurrent duplicate: two in-flight identical requests → exactly one effect and the same durable answer; after the first rolls back, the duplicate proceeds as the first

configuration of the operating limits: the api pool stays inside the four-connection budget (R43), the proxy hop count is explicit outside LOCAL (R34), request, socket and shutdown deadlines are bounded (R35, R36), the migrator's limits are read with migrations on start (R37), and its password is never configuration (R44) nor accepted by the serving process, whose migrations on start are LOCAL only (N7)

R44/N7: bootstrap never holds the owner's credential in an environment — it refuses KAURO_DB_MIGRATOR_PASSWORD by name before anything opens; LOCAL migrations on start read the password from a file, and it is no part of the configuration the running process keeps

N7: a serving process (node dist/src/main.js) given the owner's password in its environment exits 1 before it listens, naming the variable and never the value; the one-shot job (node dist/src/migrate.js) migrates a fresh database, exits 0, and a second run applies nothing
N7 (Linux): the initial environment block of a running serving process holds no migrator secret — /proc/<pid>/environ of node dist/src/main.js migrating on start from a password file

skipped.message: the initial environment block is read from /proc/<pid>/environ, which only Linux (the deployment OS) provides

testcase.name: R34: one client address cannot rotate identities past the per-address creation window of the running api — twenty verified identities are admitted, the next is 429 CREATION_RATE_LIMITED, and a forged X-Forwarded-For moves nothing when no proxy hop is trusted
R36: a request that stalls is not held forever — past the request timeout it is answered REQUEST_TIMEOUT and closed; a silent socket is closed past the connection timeout

R35: shutdown drains — the in-flight command is answered with Connection: close, a request completed on an open connection meanwhile is a 503 problem, readiness reports DRAINING, and close() ends with the in-flight work instead of waiting for keep-alive sockets
R35: the shutdown deadline is kept — a command blocked past it has its connection closed and shutdown() returns DEADLINE_EXCEEDED; the close completes once the database lets the command go
R37: with migrations on start, a database host that accepts and never answers refuses the start within the migrator's connect timeout

R42 and R38: /livez and /readyz outside /api/v1 — readiness verifies a connection and the schema against the shipped migrations (503 when drifted or behind, tolerant of a newer expand); a database outage is visible by correlation id in the unavailable and not-ready sinks and in the pool sink, never with a credential

N13: every listed outcome of every served command passes the send guard of its route — with its field codes and its current version — and a problem outside the catalogue, a field code or a current the entry does not list, or a missing current it always carries, is refused

N13: every failure site of the pipeline (transport, runtime, admission, authorizer, assurance verifier) and of each handler is an entry of the catalogue of every command that reaches it — read from the sources, with each non-literal reason resolved
N13/N16: every failure site of the reads (queries/reads.ts) is an entry of the read catalogues — the tenant-scoped decisions of every agency read, the query and cursor refusals of every list

N13: a command route never answers a problem its catalogue does not list — a collaborator's failure that the vocabulary knows but WithdrawApproval does not (PAYMENT_PENDING, or PLAN_NOT_APPROVED without its current version) answers 422 RESPONSE_CONTRACT_VIOLATION, the sink receives the violation, and nothing committed

N13: the deployable edition's own outcome of RevisePlan and ApprovePlan is in their catalogues — with the edition's collaborators (no plan services bound) both answer 422 INTEGRITY_FAILURE PLAN_SERVICES_UNAVAILABLE, nothing is journaled, and no violation reaches the sink
R1/R8 DENY: a nonexistent agency and an existing foreign agency answer byte-equal problems on a path-scoped and on a header-scoped route; no journal row, no effect, nothing in any agency's stream

R2 DENY: an unverified or disabled outsider writes nothing into another agency's security stream; its denial is a fact of its own identity stream naming the agency it selected; an unverified member's denial stays in its agency's stream

R7/R12 DENY: an idempotent replay is answered only to a caller who is still authorized — suspended 403, revoked 404, each recorded; a conflicting body gets the same refusal; reactivated, the replay is the original answer byte for byte

R7 control (recovery kept): a CMD025 replay needs the approver's current membership and role, not a fresh step-up — after the proof aged past the freshness window the replay still returns the journaled approval, while a new approval with that proof is ASSURANCE_REQUIRED

R9 RACE: a command in flight holds its actor's membership — a revocation issued meanwhile waits until the approval commits; a revocation, suspension or role change committed first makes the command wait on the membership and then refuses it

R16 DENY: the authorizer consults the stored identity state — a member whose identity row is DISABLED is refused IDENTITY_DISABLED although the token says ACTIVE, CreateAgency likewise, and nothing re-enables the row; enabled again, the member is admitted

R26: an unauthenticated command, a non-member probe and an identity-status denial each leave one durable DENY fact of the right shape; CMD001 records the owner grant and CMD025 the step-up as ALLOW facts in the agency's stream, and a replay records nothing

R18 DENY: CMD026 checks the approval controller before version and state — a non-controlling APPROVER is NOT_APPROVAL_CONTROLLER (recorded) with a stale version and on a WITHDRAWN plan; the controller and an OWNER get the version and state answers; a plan that never carried an approval answers its state

N1 RACE: a disable issued by the platform while CreateAgency is in flight waits for it and survives — the command's identity sync never writes the security status back; a disable committed first refuses the command
N1: the identity a disable restricts cannot lift it — its own runtime session is refused (42501) and every command stays IDENTITY_DISABLED; only the platform re-enables it
N3 RACE: a revocation queued behind a member's in-flight command is never overtaken by that member's later commands — the next command waits behind it and is refused NOT_A_MEMBER
N11: a VIEWER's own runtime session cannot make itself OWNER in the database — the promotion is refused (KA010) and the VIEWER still cannot archive a client through the route
N10: a compiled body whose claimed hash is not its KAURO_PLAN_BODY_V1 digest is refused 422 INTEGRITY_FAILURE BODY_DIGEST_MISMATCH — no successor, nothing superseded, no journal row
N10: a compiled body moved to another source is refused 400 INVALID_REQUEST PATCH_EFFECT_NOT_PERMITTED on decisionPatchArtifactRef — a typed patch edits decisions, never the plan's subject
N10 positive neighbour: an honest compilation is stored with the digest the repository computes, and the successor keeps the predecessor's subjects

N16 ListAgencies: GET /agencies lists only the caller's actual memberships — ACTIVE with its capabilities, SUSPENDED with none, never an INVITED one or another person's — and pages them with a cursor bound to the caller

N16 GetAgency: the safe agency view for every ACTIVE member with its own capabilities; a foreign and a nonexistent agency answer the same 404 with the denial recorded in the caller's own stream; SUSPENDED, INVITED and unauthenticated callers are refused

N16 ListMembers: team information appropriate to the caller — a team manager sees every membership with its lifecycle times, any other member only the ACTIVE team's roles; nobody sees another person's identity reference, assurance policy or security evidence

N16 ListClients and R2-060: safe client summaries with each caller's permitted actions, pages bound to the caller, the agency and the list — a cursor of agency A presented for agency B, by another caller, edited, or of another list is CURSOR_INVALID without a row or a total

N16 GetProject: the project with its current revision summary, its readiness blockers and no permitted action of this edition, under the agency selector; another agency's project answers the same 404 as one that does not exist
N16 permitted actions on the command replies: derived from the caller's role, the resource's state and the approval's control
N16: every read answers only the outcomes of its catalogue — each listed problem passes its route's send guard and an unlisted one is refused
R2-059: POST /clients/{id}/projects with verified=true and agencyOwner=true is 400 INVALID_REQUEST UNKNOWN_FIELD before any transaction; a valid neighbour body creates the project
R2-058: a string "false" where a boolean is expected is INVALID_REQUEST (type), never coerced; a missing approval member is never defaulted

manual-10 admission order: content type, size, syntax and duplicate keys, schema, idempotency key, path id, agency selector, then the authenticated subject — each answers its reason, the first failure wins, and no unit of work opens (an unauthenticated refusal opens only the one that records it)
the correlation id is echoed when supplied, generated otherwise, and present on every problem; unknown routes and methods are NOT_FOUND problems
exactly the seven catalogue routes are registered as POST and the five manual-10 reads as GET, under /api/v1
an unexpected exception is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR with only the correlation id, RETRY_SAME_KEY and the safe classification handed to the sink; no stack, SQL or message reaches the wire

N6: every label member refuses exactly the Unicode control characters (C0, DEL and C1) at the closed schema — 400 SCHEMA_VIOLATION naming the field — before any unit of work; the database refuses the same characters, and other non-ASCII text is a label

R23: a success reply its route's contract refuses is never sent — a member a collaborator adds to the ArchiveClient view is answered 422 INTEGRITY_FAILURE under the correlation id, and the sink receives the violation (path and code, never the value)

R23: a problem its contract refuses is never sent — a collaborator failure carrying a raw value beside its field error and a reason outside the vocabulary answers 422 INTEGRITY_FAILURE; the withdrawal rolled back

R23: every served route declares its replies (the route inventory the OpenAPI checker reads); a route that declares none refuses to register; a reply whose declared schema the validator never compiled, or whose body is sent as text instead of a checked object, is refused like any other violation
R29: the approval the routes answer carries actorId, and a consumer recomputes approvalHash from the wire DTO alone — when approved and after withdrawal

N17: every served command against every role — OWNER, ADMIN, OPERATOR, APPROVER, BILLING, VIEWER, a SUSPENDED and an INVITED member, a member of another agency: each role the registry role does not admit is refused with its reason and a durable DENY fact in the right stream and no effect, and each admitted role succeeds through the same route

N17: CreateAgency is identity-scoped — every verified identity creates its draft agency whatever its memberships elsewhere (an ADMIN, a BILLING, a SUSPENDED and an INVITED member of A, a member of another agency), and a disabled identity is refused with its durable fact

the validator the api composes is closed: exactly the contract names, the request schema ids, the response schema ids and Problem; it has no compile entry, and an unknown schema id is INTEGRITY_FAILURE before the input is read
customer target metadata that looks like a JSON Schema is validated as data by the application-owned TargetContract schema and never compiled
through the served routes, schema-shaped request members are refused before any unit of work opens, and a label that spells a JSON Schema is stored and answered verbatim
CMD001 CreateAgency: success, a closed-schema refusal, the database's one-DRAFT refusal and an unexpected exception carry no sentinel
CMD009 CreateClient: success, a closed-schema refusal, a foreign processing authority and an unexpected exception carry no sentinel
CMD010 ArchiveClient: success, a closed-schema refusal, a stale version and an unexpected exception carry no sentinel
CMD011 CreateProject: success, a closed-schema refusal, an unoffered mode and an unexpected exception carry no sentinel
CMD023 RevisePlan: success (the successor body carries a sentinel), a closed-schema refusal, a stale version and an unexpected exception carry no sentinel
CMD025 ApprovePlan and CMD026 WithdrawApproval: success, closed-schema refusals, a stale step-up, a non-controller and unexpected exceptions carry no sentinel — the step-up proof never comes back
no sentinel, secret, internal column value or diagnostic text of any tenant appears in any reply the seven routes sent
R28: a client correlation id that is not an id never refuses the command — the server mints a UUIDv7, answers and records the command under it, and never echoes the client value

R45: the request log's id is the correlation id — supplied or minted, every log line of a request carries the id its answer names, the internal-error sink uses the same id, and an answer below HTTP is logged under its id too

N8: a framework-error answer (an undecodable URL) is logged like every request — one 'incoming request' and one 'request completed' line with the status it was answered, under the correlation id its problem names

N15: every reply is private — Cache-Control: no-store on command successes and replays, problems of every layer (pipeline, not-found route, framework error, media type), the liveness and readiness probes, and an answer written below HTTP

R39: framework errors are problems — an undecodable URL is REQUEST_MALFORMED, an over-long path parameter PATH_ID_INVALID, an unreadable request line REQUEST_MALFORMED; each with a correlation id and nothing echoed

R40: the body is strict UTF-8 — invalid bytes are JSON_SYNTAX with Content-Length and when chunked, nothing is stored with U+FFFD; a body shorter or longer than its Content-Length is REQUEST_MALFORMED

R41: a repeated Authorization, Content-Type, Idempotency-Key, X-Correlation-Id or X-Kauro-Agency is refused as HEADER_REPEATED before any value is used — a second bearer token cannot choose the acting subject

R34: the client address reaches the creation limiter as a keyed hash of its network — through exactly the configured proxy hops; N+1 identities from one client are limited, another client is not, and a forged X-Forwarded-For moves nothing when no hop is trusted
